title: Before publishing a finding about another implementation, rule out our own bug first
description:
The one real cost of mimid acting as a conformance implementation, kept
from decision mimid-7yn7.1 (closed: provider and referee are not a
trade). Not engineering hours: accuracy.

Decision mimid-1wgh.52 item 2 already has mimid telling peers they are
wrong and citing the section, and that is how several Haven fixes
happened. It works because Jason answers email and a mistake costs an
exchange. Under a mandate, a published finding about a gatekeeper that
turns out to be our own bug is a retraction, and the asymmetry is
against us: they have lawyers and we have a bead tracker.

EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS A REAL RISK, all from one session, 2026-11-22,
all mine:

1. "No mimid1._mimi TXT record exists for mimi.reviewcommit.com."
   False. dig was not installed after the machine move and the checks
   ran with 2>/dev/null, so "command not found" read as NXDOMAIN. The
   record existed, resolved on every nameserver, and was DNSSEC-valid.
2. "Haven publishes no MIMI key record." False. I queried
   mimid1._mimi.havenmessenger.com: our selector, and missing the extra
   "mimi." label. Theirs is haven1._mimi.mimi.havenmessenger.com and is
   DNSSEC-signed.
3. "Haven's client certificate needs a dNSName SAN, not just a CN."
   Already compliant. I had tested with a certificate I generated
   myself with only a CN, and read its correct rejection as a finding
   about them. Their cert has SAN DNS:mimi.havenmessenger.com and EKU
   clientAuth, and tools/interop/haven/certs/PROVENANCE recorded that
   when Jason posted it.
4. "Haven's directory is malformed / names `message` where we use
   `submitMessage`." Overstated. All nine protocol-07 §5.1 top-level
   templates are present and match ours; the `endpoints` object is an
   additional vendor member, not a conflict.

Four for four, in one day, against a cooperative peer. Every one would
have reached Jason if the email had been sent before checking.

THE RULE, which is what this bead is for: before a finding about
another implementation leaves this repo, rule out our own bug.
Concretely, and each of these would have caught one of the above:

- Prove the tool ran. Never read empty output as a negative result;
  check the exit status or run once without silencing stderr. Already a
  memory: empty-output-is-not-a-finding.
- Check the identifier against THEIR published spelling, not ours. A
  selector, a label, a port and a path are all theirs to choose.
- When a test fixture is involved, verify the fixture is valid before
  blaming the peer. A self-signed certificate missing a SAN proves
  nothing about anyone else.
- Confirm by a second, independent path. Listing Epik's zone caught
  finding 1; reading their PROVENANCE file caught finding 3.
- Say what was observed and what was inferred, separately.

This is also why the existing rules are load-bearing and should not be
relaxed: every upstream post needs Mark's per-action OK
(peer-contributing-rules), and each finding is a bead with the draft
section cited. Those are the backstop that caught all four here.
